stem: The Pahari schools of painting developed in the __________ region.
solution: Pahari ('of the hills') painting developed in the sub-Himalayan hill states.

stem: The word 'Pahari' means __________.
solution: 'Pahari' means 'of the hills', referring to the Himalayan foothill states.

stem: The two most important Pahari schools are Basohli and __________.
solution: The two most important Pahari schools are Basohli and Kangra.

stem: The Basohli school is famous for its __________ style.
options: bold, intense colours and vigorous line
solution: The Basohli school is known for bold, intense colour and vigorous, expressive line.

stem: A striking feature of Basohli painting is the use of __________ to depict jewellery.
solution: Basohli painting famously used iridescent beetle-wing cases to depict green jewels.

stem: The Kangra school is famous for its __________ style.
solution: The Kangra school is known for its soft, lyrical, delicate and naturalistic style.

stem: The Kangra school flourished under the patronage of Raja __________.
solution: The Kangra school flourished under Raja Sansar Chand.

stem: A favourite theme of Kangra painting is the love of __________.
solution: The love of Radha and Krishna is a favourite Kangra theme.

stem: The text most often illustrated in Kangra painting is the __________.
solution: The Gita Govinda (love of Radha and Krishna) was a favourite Kangra text.

stem: The Guler school is regarded as the __________ of the Kangra style.
solution: The Guler school is considered the cradle/forerunner of the Kangra style.

stem: Pahari painting is a form of __________ art.
solution: Pahari painting is a miniature art form.

stem: The Pahari style developed partly through artists trained in the __________ tradition.
solution: Mughal-trained artists migrating to the hills helped shape the Pahari (esp. Guler-Kangra) style.

stem: The women in Kangra painting are shown with __________.
options: delicate features, graceful bodies and refined charm
solution: Kangra women are depicted with delicate features, graceful forms and refined charm.

stem: The landscapes in Kangra painting are usually __________.
solution: Kangra landscapes are lush, green and naturalistic, reflecting the hill environment.

stem: The Basohli school flourished mainly in the __________ century.
solution: The Basohli school flourished mainly in the 17th century.

stem: The Kangra school flourished mainly in the late __________ century.
solution: The Kangra school flourished in the late 18th and early 19th centuries.

stem: An illustrated Pahari text on the moods of love is the __________.
solution: The Rasamanjari, on the sentiments of love, was illustrated in the Basohli school.

stem: Pahari painting is largely __________ in theme.
solution: Pahari painting is largely Hindu devotional and romantic, especially Vaishnava (Krishna) themes.

stem: The Basohli painting uses a __________ background typically.
solution: Basohli painting often uses a bold red or intense colour background.

stem: The 'Nayika' and 'Barahmasa' themes also appear in Pahari painting, showing shared __________ subjects.
solution: Pahari painting shares the Nayika and Barahmasa poetic themes of Rajput painting.

stem: The Pahari artists belonged to hereditary families of painters called __________.
solution: Pahari painters often came from hereditary artisan families (e.g. the Guler family of Pandit Seu).

stem: The famous family of Pahari painters was headed by __________.
options: Pandit Seu (and his sons Manaku and Nainsukh)
solution: The famous Guler family of Pandit Seu, and his sons Manaku and Nainsukh, shaped Pahari painting.

stem: Nainsukh, a celebrated Pahari painter, worked for the court of __________.
solution: Nainsukh served the court of Balwant Singh of Jasrota.

stem: The Pahari painting style is distinguished by its __________ quality.
solution: Pahari painting has a lyrical, poetic quality.

stem: The soft colours and flowing lines of the Kangra style suited the depiction of __________.
solution: The soft Kangra style suited tender romantic and devotional themes.

stem: The Pahari schools were patronised by __________.
options: Rajput rulers of the hill states
solution: Pahari painting was patronised by the Rajput rulers of the hill states.

stem: The 'Bhagavata Purana' illustrated in Pahari style narrates the story of __________.
solution: The Bhagavata Purana, illustrated in Pahari style, narrates the life of Krishna.

stem: Compared with Basohli, the Kangra style is __________.
solution: The Kangra style is softer and more refined than the bold Basohli style.

stem: The Pahari painters used colours made from __________.
options: minerals, vegetables and even beetle wings/gold
solution: Pahari colours came from minerals, vegetables and materials like beetle wings and gold.

stem: The graceful female figure of Kangra painting is often set in a __________.
solution: Kangra heroines are often set in moonlit gardens or by riverbanks.

stem: The theme of 'Abhisarika Nayika', a woman going to meet her lover, appears in __________ painting.
solution: The Abhisarika Nayika theme appears in Pahari and Rajasthani painting.

stem: The Pahari schools together belong to the broader tradition of __________ painting.
solution: The Pahari schools belong to the broader Rajput (Hindu miniature) tradition.

stem: The Pahari painting is admired for expressing __________ delicately.
solution: Pahari painting delicately expresses human emotion and mood.

stem: The centres of Pahari painting include Basohli, Guler, Kangra, Chamba and __________.
solution: Garhwal was another important Pahari painting centre.

stem: The typical Pahari painting depicts figures with __________ eyes.
solution: Pahari figures typically have large, lotus-shaped, expressive eyes.

stem: The refined naturalism of the Kangra style owed much to __________ influence.
solution: The Kangra style's refined naturalism owed much to late Mughal influence.

stem: The Pahari school reflects the __________ of the Himalayan hill courts.
solution: Pahari painting reflects the devotional and cultural life of the hill courts.

stem: The vivid green of foliage and the misty hills are characteristic of the __________ landscape.
solution: Vivid green foliage and misty hills characterise the Kangra landscape.

stem: The Basohli school's intense expressive style makes it one of the __________ Pahari schools.
solution: Basohli is one of the earliest and most distinctive Pahari schools.

stem: The Pahari painting tradition declined with the decline of the __________.
solution: Pahari painting declined with the fall of the hill states and British expansion.

stem: The Pahari painters excelled at depicting the __________ associated with the seasons and love.
solution: Pahari painters excelled at depicting the moods (rasa) of seasons and love.

stem: The Kangra painting is considered a __________ of Indian miniature art.
solution: The Kangra school is regarded as a high point of Indian miniature painting.

stem: The main difference between Basohli and Kangra painting is in their __________.
options: colour intensity and line (bold vs soft)
solution: Basohli is bold and intense, while Kangra is soft and refined — the chief stylistic difference.

stem: The Pahari painting typically portrays love in a __________ setting.
solution: Pahari painting portrays love in natural, idyllic settings.

stem: The refined Kangra female type is sometimes considered the __________ of Indian painting.
solution: The Kangra female type is regarded as an ideal of feminine grace in Indian painting.

stem: The Pahari painting made important use of __________ backgrounds in the Kangra phase.
solution: The Kangra phase made important use of naturalistic landscape backgrounds.

stem: The Pahari schools are a major branch of Indian __________ painting.
solution: The Pahari schools are a major branch of Indian miniature painting.

stem: The lyrical Kangra depictions of the Gita Govinda beautifully express __________.
solution: The Kangra Gita Govinda paintings express divine love (Radha-Krishna).

stem: The overall importance of the Pahari schools is their contribution of __________ to Indian art.
solution: The Pahari schools contributed lyrical grace and refined emotional expression to Indian art.

stem: The Pahari and Rajasthani schools together form the two great branches of __________ painting.
solution: The Pahari (hill) and Rajasthani (plains) schools are the two great branches of Rajput painting.

stem: The Basohli school's brilliant colours were often set off by borders of __________.
solution: Basohli paintings typically have deep red borders framing the intense colours.

stem: The Basohli painters depicted green jewels using fragments of __________.
solution: Basohli painters used iridescent beetle-wing cases to depict emerald-green jewels.

stem: The Guler school is regarded as the transitional link that led to the __________ style.
solution: The Guler school is the transitional link leading to the refined Kangra style.

stem: The Pahari painter Nainsukh was the son of __________.
solution: Nainsukh was the son of Pandit Seu of the famous Guler painter family.

stem: The refined naturalism of the Kangra style was shaped by the arrival of __________-trained artists.
solution: Mughal-trained artists migrating to the hills shaped the naturalistic Guler-Kangra style.

stem: The Kangra painting reached its peak under Raja Sansar Chand of __________.
solution: The Kangra school peaked under Raja Sansar Chand of Kangra.

stem: The Pahari painters most often illustrated the love of __________.
solution: The Pahari painters most often illustrated the love of Radha and Krishna.

stem: The Basohli painting of the 'Rasamanjari' illustrates the theme of __________.
solution: The Rasamanjari, illustrated in Basohli, deals with the sentiments of love.

stem: The Kangra style is admired for its __________ depiction of the female form.
solution: The Kangra style is admired for its graceful, idealised female form.

stem: Pahari painting centres include Basohli, Guler, Kangra, Chamba, Garhwal and __________.
solution: Kullu and Mandi were among the other Pahari painting centres.

stem: The Kangra painters set their romantic scenes against __________ backgrounds.
solution: Kangra painters used lush green, naturalistic hill backgrounds.

stem: The Gita Govinda and Bhagavata Purana illustrated in Pahari style celebrate __________.
solution: These texts celebrate Krishna's life and divine love.

stem: The Basohli style is one of the __________ Pahari schools.
solution: Basohli is one of the earliest and most distinctive Pahari schools.

stem: The Pahari painters came largely from __________ families.
solution: The Pahari painters came largely from hereditary artisan families like the Guler family.

stem: The overall mood of the Kangra painting is __________.
solution: The Kangra painting has a lyrical, tender and romantic mood.

stem: The Pahari schools are the __________ branch of Rajput painting.
solution: The Pahari schools form the hill (Himalayan) branch of Rajput painting.

stem: The theme of a heroine waiting through the seasons for her lover is the __________ subject, common in Pahari art.
solution: The Barahmasa (twelve months) theme of a longing heroine is common in Pahari painting.

stem: The Pahari painting declined with the weakening of the __________ under British expansion.
solution: Pahari painting declined with the weakening of the hill states under British expansion.
